rows.evidence: Q1: Methods/Results, Table 1 - the authors train AlexNet and GoogLeNet on 54,306 PlantVillage leaf images across 60 configurations and report their own accuracy/F1 results (best 99.35% on held-out test set; ~31% on external web images).
rows.notes: The study is a primary image-classification experiment, but not on the claimed technology or effect. Images are single leaves photographed under controlled conditions (homogeneous background, facing up), not UAV or other remote-sensing imagery; the authors themselves note they are constrained to single-leaf images and that accuracy drops to ~31% on images from other conditions. The model classifies crop-disease pairs (presence/identity of disease), it does not grade infection severity, does not address detection before canopy-wide symptoms, and reports nothing on targeted responses or pest control outcomes. At most it supports the precondition (disease identification from leaf images) for the claimed control effect. The Discussion explicitly says early-stage diagnosis by visual symptoms is challenging and the tool is meant to supplement, not replace, lab diagnosis.

notes: Full text available and complete. Study concerns deep CNN classification of leaf photographs (PlantVillage dataset), not remote sensing/UAV imagery; no field, severity-grading or management-response data are reported.
